study.title: Repeated acupuncture treatments modulate amygdala resting state functional connectivity of depressive patients
study.study_design: Randomized, sham-controlled trial with two parallel arms; resting-state fMRI collected before first and last treatments
study.randomization: Patients were randomized into verum acupuncture plus fluoxetine or sham acupuncture plus fluoxetine group
study.blinding: Participants wore masks over their eyes during treatment; sham procedure designed to mimic verum without needle insertion; blinding level of practitioners and outcome assessors not explicitly stated
study.population: Female patients with major depressive disorder, aged 30-60 years old, recruited through community postings
study.inclusion_criteria: 1) Women who met the criteria of depression in ICD-10; 2) standard score of Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) >= 53 or total score of Montgomery-Asberg depression rating scale (MADRS) >= 14; 3) aged 30-60 years old and able to provide voluntary informed consent; 4) right-handed; 5) primary school education or higher; and 6) normal cognitive functioning, with no aphasia or intellectual disabilities.
study.exclusion_criteria: 1) Refused to sign informed content; 2) pregnant or lactating women; 3) women with metallic implants; 4) used antipsychotics or antidepressants within a month before the study; 5) consumption of alcohol or illicit substances; 6) patients with severe damage of liver or kidney function, or with neurological deficits, rheumatologic disorders, cardiac disease, diabetes, malignant tumors or any other significant systemic disorders that might affect the results; 7) presence of severe psychoses (schizophrenia, mania, paranoid psychosis or depression with suicidal intent) or dementia; 8) presence of any somatic diseases (such as cerebral infarction, cerebral hemorrhage, Parkinson's or cerebral tumor) or any other significant systemic disorders that might affect the results.

arms.dropouts: 4 subjects dropped out: 3 due to having had only one fMRI scan and 1 due to a scheduling conflict
6 subjects dropped out: 2 due to discomfort from treatment (headache and diarrhea), 1 due to a scheduling conflict, and 3 due to having had only one scan

conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI; subjects required to keep eyes closed, relax the mind, not fall asleep, and not to think of anything in particular

interventions.manipulation_exact: needles inserted intramuscularly to a depth of 15-20 mm and were left in situ for 20 min; no further manipulation described
interventions.session_duration_exact: 20 min (needle retention time); total session duration not separately reported

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: The advantage of abdominal acupuncture is that it only produces mild sensations, possibly making it more acceptable to patients.
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Paper did not formally measure or report deqi or sensory responses using a validated instrument. Only narrative statement about mild sensations provided.

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T2*-weighted functional images acquired with the gradient-echo EPI sequence; high-resolution structural: T1-weighted three-dimensional multi-echo magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MP-RAGE) sequence
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: functional: data matrix 64×64, field of view 240 mm, slice thickness 4 mm, interslice gap 0.88 mm, 31 slices; structural: data matrix 256×256, field of view 256 mm×256 mm, slice thickness 1 mm, 176 sagittal slices
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Two 6-minute resting-state fMRI scans (180 time points acquired in 6 min each)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: SPM8 (Statistical Parametric Mapping, Welcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK; implemented by MATLAB R2012b, Math Works, Inc., Natick, MA, USA)
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: CONN toolbox v15.g (Whitfield-Gabrieli & Nieto-Castanon, 2012); SPM8; WFU-Pick Atlas software (Maldjian et al., 2003); artifact detection toolbox (http://www.nitrc.org/projects/artifact_detect/); SPSS 19.0 Software (clinical data)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: 8 mm full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Time points in subjects' images were marked as outliers if the global signal exceeded three standard deviations from the mean or if scan-to-scan motion exceeded 0.5 mm deviation
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: brain segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for the removal of temporal confounding factors (white matter and CSF)
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: Pearson's correlation coefficients transformed into Fisher's Z-scores
statistical_thresholds_exact: voxel-wise p < 0.005 (uncorrected) and cluster-level p < 0.05 family-wise error correction

extraction_notes.note: Deqi/sensation was not formally measured or assessed using a validated instrument (e.g., MASS, MGH acupuncture sensation scale). The paper only mentions that abdominal acupuncture 'only produces mild sensations, possibly making it more acceptable to patients' as a narrative statement.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported. No validated instruments (e.g., CEQ, AEQ) were used. The paper does not mention these measures.
Allocation guessing (whether participants correctly guessed their treatment assignment) was not assessed or reported.

The exact number of sessions per participant in the verum and sham groups is not explicitly stated as a numeric total. The frequency was once daily for first 3 days then once every 3 days for remainder of 8-week trial, making the total calculable but not explicitly reported.

No correlation analysis was reported between the right amygdala - left Para/Pu rsFC change and clinical outcomes (MADRS/SDS). The correlation was only reported for the left amygdala - sgACC/pgACC rsFC change.

The paper refers to 'sham acupuncture' and 'verum acupuncture' but the sham involves no needle penetration at the same body locations (abdominal acupoints) using empty plastic sheaths tapped on skin. The nature of the tactile stimulation provided by this sham is not further quantified.

The Table 1 heading says 'Acupuncture mean (SD)' and 'Sham mean (SD).' The SDS pre-treatment value for the verum group is reported as '47.833 (6.46)' in the table - the exact value with three decimal places is preserved as reported.

Within-group change statistics for verum group MADRS/SDS are not explicitly reported. The paper states 'paired t-test comparing pre and post-treatment clinical outcomes also indicates that the symptoms in the sham acupuncture plus fluoxetine group significantly decreased after treatment (MADRS: p < 0.001; SDS: p < 0.001)' but corresponding statistics for the verum group are not separately stated in the results section.
The paper states the depth was '15-20 mm' for needle insertion; a single numeric value cannot be specified for depth_mm_numeric without guessing, so this field was left null.

The laterality of some bilateral acupoints (Shangqu KL17, Huaroumen ST24, Qipang extra-point) is inferred from Fig. 1 showing bilateral placement. The paper lists them once in the text but Fig. 1 shows them bilaterally. This inference is noted.

The paper uses the abbreviation 'Para/Pu' in the table header as 'parahippocampus; Pu, putamen' - these are clustered together as a single result cluster based on the single coordinate row reported. The cluster encompasses both structures.

The paper states 'The strength of the amygdala-sgACC/pgACC rsFC was positively associated with corresponding clinical improvement (as indicated by a negative correlation with MADRS and SDS scores).' The positive association with clinical improvement and negative correlation with scores reflects improvement (lower scores = better). This is preserved as reported.

Table 2 column header says 'Regions showed significantly increased resting-state functional connectivity' but the sham group row shows Post-treatment < pre-treatment (decreased rsFC). The table title may be imprecisely worded or inclusive of all within-group changes reported.

There is no placebo fluoxetine arm. The paper acknowledges this limitation: 'there is no placebo fluoxetine, which prevents us from exploring the effect and mechanism of fluoxetine as well as the interaction between fluoxetine and acupuncture.'
The paper does not report flip angle separately for functional sequence (stated as 90°) and structural (15°). Both are reported in the methods section.
The coordinate space is stated to be MNI space in the table header. No conversion was required or performed.
The study only recruited female patients, which limits generalizability. Authors acknowledge this and state external validity may only be applied to female patients.
